notes.summary: Mathematical PASS for L0–L5: actual positive-real all-face balance gives uniform closed-cell Lipschitz bounds and supports on entire incident cells. No compactness, positive growth or PA gluing is inferred.
notes.detailedSummary: The independent reconstruction proves rational feasible-perspective density, active-normal distance bounds and uniform insets, saturated-covolume stationary flux, both-sign generator bounds, exclusion of minus-infinite derivatives, a finite sublinear infimum over all incident directions, and induction over every face and every relative subgradient. The resulting bound is A_X C+B_X G. The path consequence uses intrinsic polygonal distance.
notes.text:
Mathematical verdict: PASS for the unchanged scoped Lipschitz theorem under its stated hypotheses. Let X be finite, pure-dimensional and globally embedded with rational cells and all closed faces. Actual strictly positive REAL top weights balance at every codimension-one face, including otherwise boundary faces. A fixed rational refinement carries continuous actual REAL cellwise-affine gamma. Let G be the maximum intrinsic norm of its affine gradients. Assume f is finite, continuous, printed-PC and |f-gamma|<=C. Neither compactness nor positive growth nor PC of gamma is required. Refinement inherits balance: newly inserted facets have equal opposite contributions, and inherited facets retain the original equation.

The elementary foundations were reconstructed. A nonnegative representation by finitely many columns can be reduced to independent active columns: subtract a multiple of a dependence until one positive coefficient vanishes, then repeat. The finitely many independent inverses give sum coefficients<=K||v||. This proves closedness of a finite generated cone by taking a subsequence with one active subset and bounded convergent coefficients. Nearest-point first variation separates a point outside such a cone. Finite polyhedral generation follows by removing the joint-kernel lineality, taking the bounded level-one section of the sum of nonnegative inequality rows, and decomposing that bounded polyhedron into vertices by increasing active rank. Homogenization gives vertex hull plus recession cone. Rational systems give rational points and rays. Fourier-Motzkin elimination proves that finite linear images are closed polyhedra and that rational projections remain rational.

A finite convex function on a relative open neighborhood is locally Lipschitz: cube vertices bound it above, reflection bounds it below on a smaller cube, and extended secants bound slopes. Relative subgradients exist by projecting points immediately below its closed local epigraph and taking limiting unit supporting normals. The limiting vertical component is negative; a nonzero horizontal support cannot attain an extremum at the center of a full relative spatial neighborhood. Division gives an affine support, and convex secants extend it throughout the convex domain. On full affine space this also proves finite-function biconjugacy through the supremum of affine supports.

L0. For a feasible PCC discard zero coefficients and put t_i=alpha_i x_i. Constraints alpha_i>0, sum alpha_i=1, A_i t_i<=alpha_i b_i, and sum t_i in the common face are rational linear constraints. In the minimal feasible face, rational row reduction supplies a rational particular solution and rational kernel basis. Approximation within that affine space preserves positive coefficients and strict inactive inequalities. The rational endpoints t_i/alpha_i and rational centers converge to the actual tuple. Printed inequalities and continuity therefore give every real-endpoint PCC, including a possible irrational limiting center. The common face may be the cell itself, yielding ordinary convexity on every inherited closed cell. No automatic continuity assertion is used.

L1. For P={x:A_i x<=b_i}, let z be nearest to x and w=x-z. The active outward normals generate w. Otherwise separating their cone gives v with A_i v<=0 on active rows and <w,v>>0; inactive slack makes z+tv feasible for small positive t, contradicting nearest-point first variation. Independent-column reduction gives sum lambda_i<=H||w||. Hence ||w||²=sum lambda_i(A_i x-b_i)<=H||w|| max_i(A_i x-b_i)_+, proving dist(x,P)<=H max violation uniformly, including unbounded polyhedra.

Restrict every row from every incident cell and from the face tau to tau. A valid affine inequality either vanishes identically there or is strictly slack throughout its relative interior. Choose a rational interior anchor and rational delta smaller than every nonidentical slack. Tightening those rows by delta gives a nonempty rational inset. At every y in tau its violation is at most delta, so the distance bound supplies inset z with ||z-y||<=D_tau uniformly. Empty row lists use D_tau=0. Choose finite rational generators for each incident cone, including both lineality signs. At an actual face their lineality is T_tau; the proof requires its inclusion. Identically active rows obey the generator constraints, and all remaining rows have margin delta. A single positive rational epsilon_tau makes z+epsilon_tau v_j feasible in every generator's assigned cell simultaneously, at every inset point. These constants depend only on geometry.

L2. For saturated corank-one N_rho in N_sigma, a facet basis followed by a primitive inward quotient lift is a cell lattice basis. Its perpendicular height is c_sigma/c_rho, where c is Euclidean covolume and c_point=1. Thus density mu_sigma=w_sigma c_sigma converts primitive balance into stationary unit-conormal flux without rounding actual weights. If the convex conical hull of the star were proper in its span E, closedness and nearest-point separation give lambda>=0 on the star and positive somewhere. Apply the divergence theorem to the tangent projection of its constant gradient on each top cone truncated by a ball. Divergence is zero; weighted planar-facet flux cancels by balance. Spherical flux is lambda(x)/||x||, nonnegative everywhere and strictly positive on an angular patch of some top cell. Positive densities contradict zero total flux. Dimension one is endpoint cancellation, dimension zero has E={0}, and lineality is allowed. Consequently fixed generators span E positively. Independent-column reduction gives one finite K_tau with coefficient sum<=K_tau||v|| for BOTH v and -v.

L3. Assume f|tau has global Lipschitz constant M_tau. At y in its relative interior choose inset z and xi=z-y. Incident right directional derivatives h_sigma(w) initially lie in [-infinity,infinity), never +infinity because a finite positive secant exists. They are homogeneous and subadditive by midpoint convexity; tangential derivatives have absolute value<=M_tau||xi||. The same-cell secant at y+xi+epsilon v_j gives h_sigma(xi+epsilon v_j)<=2C+G(D_tau+epsilon||v_j||). Subadditivity using -xi gives h_sigma(v_j)<=U_tau=[2C+(G+M_tau)D_tau]/epsilon_tau+G V_tau.

Every finite assigned zero-sum incident-direction list has feasible endpoints for one sufficiently small common t. Real PCC centered at y gives a nonnegative sum of difference quotients. If any h_sigma(w) were -infinity, append a fixed-generator representation of -w. All appended quotients have finite upper limits bounded by their coefficients times U_tau; the sum would tend to -infinity. Thus every incident derivative is finite, and every finite zero-sum list has nonnegative total derivative cost.

Define H_y(v) as the infimum of total derivative cost over ALL finite assigned incident directions summing to v. Fixed generators give H_y(v)<=K_tau U_tau||v||. Appending their representation of -v gives H_y(v)>=-K_tau U_tau||v||. Concatenation and scaling prove subadditivity and positive homogeneity, with H_y(0)=0. Both-sign bounds imply Lipschitzness. A subgradient at zero therefore supplies p.v<=H_y(v), ||p||<=K_tau U_tau. Orthogonal extension gives a full ambient vector of the same norm. For every x in every entire incident closed cell, p.(x-y)<=H_y(x-y)<=h_sigma(x-y)<=f(x)-f(y). This is a simultaneous whole-cell support, not a one-cell or sampled substitute.

L4–L5. Induct over ALL face dimensions. Previously constructed supports of norm<=B at proper-face points support the whole current face tau. At q in its relative interior take ANY relative subgradient a. Follow the ray in direction a/||a||. If it exits at finite endpoint z, closedness puts z in a proper face, and t||a||<=f(z)-f(q)<=tB. If it escapes forever, bounded f-gamma makes the asymptotic secant slope the affine gamma slope, at most G. Thus every relative subgradient has norm<=M_tau=max(B,G). Two interior supports give Lipschitzness; mixing closed-cell points with an interior anchor and passing to the limit gives the same global closed-cell bound. L3 then supplies its ambient supports.

Minimal positive-dimensional faces without vertices start by the escaping-ray argument. Lineality and affine cells without proper faces are included. A point face has intrinsic Lipschitz constant zero but may have nonzero ambient support bound. If proper support coefficients are A_rho C+B_rho G, set a_tau=max A_rho and b_tau=1+max B_rho, with empty maxima zero. Valid next support coefficients are A_tau=K_tau(2/epsilon_tau+a_tau D_tau/epsilon_tau) and B_tau=K_tau((1+b_tau)D_tau/epsilon_tau+V_tau). Taking finite maxima of support and Lipschitz coefficient pairs gives A_X C+B_X G. Segment summation gives the intrinsic polygonal-distance consequence. Distinct nonincident components need not satisfy an ambient-distance bound. This proves the cellwise input, not global PA gluing.

notes.detailedSummary: The unchanged maximum facet penalty and requested sum penalty both work. The McShane infimum requires no attainment. Full actual conjugate-domain continuity, rational spatial samples with real heights, exact recession rays, projected graph faces and rational matching kernels give genuine REAL-PA majorants with global error and unshifted contacts. Dyadic shifts have error [4eta,5eta] and gap3eta/2. The whole-line sqrt example has exact error sqrt2−1.
notes.text:
Mathematical verdict: PASS under the explicit single-cell hypotheses. Let sigma be a nonempty closed rational convex cell in its rational affine hull Q, ell(x)=a.x+b actual REAL affine, a.v>0 for every nonzero recession direction of sigma, and f finite continuous convex with |f-ell|<=C and an explicit global Lipschitz constant L.

C1–C2. Write facet inequalities A_j x<=b_j. The independently proved active-normal estimate gives dist(x,sigma)<=H delta(x), delta=max(0,max_j(A_jx-b_j)). The unchanged paper prints this maximum penalty. The task's sum V(x)=sum_j(A_jx-b_j)_+ also works because delta<=V. Both have rational spatial walls and vanish on the ENTIRE sigma.

Their recession penalties r(v), respectively max(0,max_j A_jv) and sum_j(A_jv)_+, vanish exactly on rec(sigma). On the compact recession unit section a.v has a positive minimum, retained in a neighborhood. On the remaining compact unit directions r has a positive minimum. A sufficiently large integer kappa therefore makes h(v)=a.v+kappa r(v)>0 on every nonzero full-hull direction. If the recession unit section is empty, use the positive minimum of r on the entire sphere; dimension zero is vacuous. Constant terms change each penalty from its homogeneous version by a bounded amount. Hence Gamma=ell+kappa V, or the printed ell+kappa delta, is coercive, convex, exact ell on sigma and rational-spatial REAL-PA.

Scalar extension is checked separately. Affine tuples on a finite rational carrier that agree on common faces satisfy rational homogeneous linear equations, tested on rational affine bases. A rational kernel basis becomes literal integral-slope/rational-constant functions after clearing denominators. The actual tuple is their finite REAL linear combination. This avoids assuming arbitrary irrational-wall maximum closure.

C3. Choose rational M>=L and define fhat(x)=inf_{y in sigma}[f(y)+M||x-y||]. A fixed y0 gives an upper bound, while Lipschitzness and the triangle inequality give the lower bound f(y0)-M||x-y0||. The infimum is finite and equals f on sigma, without assuming attainment. Approximate minimizers prove convexity; the triangle inequality proves global M-Lipschitzness. A nearest cell point gives fhat(x)<=ell(x)+C+(M+||a||)dist(x,sigma). Increase kappa to at least H(M+||a||), so fhat<=Gamma+C. Set F=max(fhat,Gamma-C). Then F is finite continuous convex on full Q, Gamma-C<=F<=Gamma+C and F=f on ALL sigma. Neither fhat nor F is asserted PA, and neither receives MA.

C4. A finite full-space convex PA function is the maximum of its affine pieces: a piece on a full-dimensional region is a global support by secants. Write Gamma=max_j(a_j.x+b_j), h=Gamma^infinity=max_j a_j.x and Delta=conv{a_j}. These are actual REAL slopes; vertices and boundary points may be irrational. Coercivity gives 0 in the interior of Delta. F-h is bounded. Therefore F*(p)=sup_x[p.x-F(x)] is finite and uniformly bounded for EVERY p in the CLOSED Delta. Outside Delta, nearest-point separation supplies v with p.v>h(v), making F*(p)=+infinity. This establishes the exact actual domain, not merely its interior or rational points.

The conjugate is convex and lower semicontinuous. Its finitely many vertex values bound it above by B. At p in Delta choose r>0 below each inactive facet slack divided by normal norm. Every feasible direction from p remains feasible to radius r: active inequalities are homogeneous, inactive ones retain slack. For nearby q, z=p+r(q-p)/||q-p|| lies in Delta, so F*(q)<=F*(p)+(||q-p||/r)(B-F*(p)). Lower semicontinuity proves continuity at all boundary points. This is a polytope argument, not a false general compact-convex continuity assertion.

Continuity of F makes rational spatial points sufficient for its conjugate supremum. At each p choose rational s giving conjugate error<eta/2. Continuity of F* gives a neighborhood with error<eta. A finite compact cover supplies rational spatial samples A, enlarged by the prescribed rational contact set, with actual REAL heights F(s), such that F*(p)-eta<=g_A(p)=max_{s in A}(p.s-F(s))<=F*(p) throughout Delta.

The rational carrier's recession cones cover Q: an unbounded subsequence on any ray lies in one cell and its inequalities force that direction into its recession cone. On each such cone h is linear. Refining all homogeneous rational row hyperplanes and coordinate orthants gives a pointed rational fan; each relatively open refined cone has constant row signs and lies in a covering recession cone. Finite cone generation yields rational spatial rays r_k and epi(h)=cone{(r_k,h(r_k)),(0,1)}. Heights are exact actual recession values. The elementary generation proof includes lineality; the fan makes the selected spatial cones pointed.

Form E_A=conv{(s,F(s)):s in A}+epi(h). Finite real elimination makes it a closed polyhedron with full spatial projection. Convex secants and bounded F-h give F(x+v)-F(x)<=h(v), so sample translates and their convex hull lie in epi(F). Upward fibers are nonempty with finite attained lower endpoints by closedness. Thus E_A=epi(P), with P finite convex continuous polyhedral.

Direct maximization over sample lifts and rays gives P*=g_A on actual Delta and +infinity outside it. Finite-function biconjugacy, independently proved in n1, yields F<=P<=F+eta GLOBALLY on Q. Lift membership and the lower inequality give exact prescribed contacts. Rec(E_A)=epi(h): one inclusion is immediate, and the reverse follows by dividing a recession sequence by its parameter, using the bounded sample hull and closed cone. Thus P^infinity=h exactly.

Every lower graph face is exposed by a functional with negative vertical component; full spatial projection excludes vertical supporting facets. It retains precisely selected sample lifts and zero-cost rays and excludes the vertical ray. Its spatial projection is the convex hull of rational positions plus the cone of rational spatial rays, hence rational despite irrational heights. Projection is injective on the graph. Supporting equalities restrict affinely on other graph faces, so intersections project to common faces. Their finite projections and faces form a rational carrying complex. The rational matching-kernel proof above gives genuine scalar-extended REAL-PA. Ordinary convexity gives PCC and ambient supports; subtracting a support's tangential extension makes residual outgoing cycle derivatives nonnegative where that test is needed.

On rec(sigma), r=0 and h(v)=a.v. Bounded f-ell has the same recession on each feasible ray. Restricting P gives above-approximants on sigma with exact actual cell recession and unshifted prescribed contacts.

The whole-line example is proved analytically: F(x)=sqrt(1+x²), samples +/-1 of height sqrt2, and P=sqrt2+max(0,|x|-1). For r=|x|<=1, P²-F²=1-r²>=0. For r>=1, P²-F²=2(sqrt2-1)(r-1)>=0. Also P-(sqrt2-1) is respectively1 or r, both<=F. The exact global error is sqrt2-1, attained at zero, independently of any grid.

C5. With eta_n=2^-n and p_n-f in [0,eta_n], set g_n=p_n+4eta_n. Then g_n-f lies in [4eta_n,5eta_n] and g_n-g_(n+1)>=3eta_n/2>0. Rational shifts preserve carriers, recession and actual-reference bounded difference. Only unshifted majorants have exact contacts.

Finite contacts do not synchronize an entire shared face. Two fine rational meshes containing a prescribed finite rational set give different chord majorants of t² on [0,1], each with maximum interval error equal to interval length²/4. Separate convex supports also need not give a common ambient support: restrictions -epsilon x on the positive ray and epsilon x on the negative ray agree at zero, but a common support requires p<=-epsilon and p>=epsilon. This is a logical failure of the gluing inference, not a claimed original global counterexample. L3 supports the original PC function, not independently selected approximants.

notes.summary: Mathematical PASS for B1–B3: the UNBALANCED orthant has sharp REAL-PA error floor1/2 and fails uniform continuity. It supplies no original balanced counterexample.
notes.detailedSummary: Geometric-mean concavity gives continuous closed-cell convexity and positive recession. Every finite continuous REAL-PA function on a convex cell is globally Lipschitz. The prescribed pairs force error>=1/2, attained by gamma+1/2. Positive-axis inward derivatives are minus-infinite, with no finite subgradient or finite open convex extension. Origin subgradients are separately characterized.
notes.text:
On x,y>0, the Hessian quadratic form of sqrt(xy) is -(y dx-x dy)²/[4(xy)^(3/2)], so the geometric mean is concave. Inward approximation and continuity extend concavity to the closed orthant. Thus b=max(0,1-sqrt(xy)) is continuous convex and lies in [0,1]. The function f=x+y+b is continuous convex with bounded difference from gamma=x+y. Its recession is v_1+v_2, strictly positive on every nonzero orthant recession direction.

Every finite continuous REAL-PA function on a convex cell is globally Lipschitz: a segment has a finite partition into carrying affine pieces; the maximum intrinsic gradient norm bounds each piece, and summing lengths gives the bound. Closed boundary segments follow by continuity. For any such approximant a, let e=||a-f||_infinity and L be a Lipschitz constant of a-gamma. At z_n=(n²,0), w_n=(n²,n^-2), b(z_n)=1, b(w_n)=0 and distance=n^-2. Hence 1<=2e+L/n². Taking n to infinity gives e>=1/2. Infinite error is harmless. The affine REAL-PA function gamma+1/2 attains exactly1/2.

The same pairs have f difference1-n^-2 at distance tending to zero, proving failure of uniform continuity and global Lipschitzness. At (x,0), x>0, the inward y quotient is 1-sqrt(x)/sqrt(t), tending to -infinity. A finite subgradient would bound it below by its finite y component, impossible. A finite convex extension to an open neighborhood would be locally Lipschitz by n1's cube argument, also impossible. The other positive axis is symmetric.

At the origin, finite subgradients are exactly p with 1-p_1>=0, 1-p_2>=0 and 4(1-p_1)(1-p_2)>=1. Near zero the supporting condition is (1-p_1)x+(1-p_2)y>=sqrt(xy). AM-GM proves sufficiency, and minimizing in x/y proves necessity. Since f>=1+x+y-sqrt(xy) globally, this condition supports globally too. Thus the origin differs from the positive-axis failure.

A single positive orthant has only one inward primitive normal at each axis and cannot balance. Its star lies in a proper halfspace, so n1's positive-flux contradiction does not apply. This is an UNBALANCED diagnostic, not an original balanced counterexample, and no MA is assigned.
